title: Sectionwise inverse image preserves independent-coefficient K-flat complexes
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with essentially small pro-etale sites, $R_Y,R_X$ commutative ring sheaves, $c:g^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$, and $F$ the additive sectionwise inverse-image module functor identified with the displayed construction. Then the induced functor on cochain complexes sends every independent-coefficient K-flat complex over $R_Y$ to an independent-coefficient K-flat complex over $R_X$.

source.place: Step 1, tensor preservation argument of lem-pod-sectionwise-flat-kflat; the indicated clause

proof.text: Present sectionwise inverse image on sheaves of sets as the inverse functor of a geometric morphism: its equivalence supplies the right adjoint and finite-limit preservation. Construct an AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses explicitly. Its ring identification is the underlying-set, ULift-valued image of c; its module functor is the given inverse-image construction; the natural identification of underlying module sheaves is the identity. Ring operation graphs are preserved by the components of c. Module addition and zero are unchanged. For the scalar graph, restriction through c inverse cancels c on each section by c.hom_inv_id.

Take the conservative set-indexed family of points of the pro-etale topos of X. For each point use its normalized RX-stalk presentation; the operations are fixed by the underlying-set comparisons. Convert the family criterion on bijective maps into JointlyReflectIsomorphisms using the equivalence between bijectivity and invertibility in Type. No nonempty-family hypothesis is introduced.

Substitute the supplied equality identifying F with the sectionwise module construction. The explicitly constructed algebraic presentation has exactly that additive module functor. Apply the arbitrary-K-flat algebraic inverse-image theorem to the geometric morphism, this presentation, and the conservative family. It gives the claimed independent-coefficient K-flat predicate for the termwise image without imposing flatness on terms or boundedness.

proof_origin.place: lemma-pullback-K-flat-points (Tag 0DEP), using the existing algebraic inverse-image implementation of the 0DEN stalk criterion; explicit sectionwise algebraic presentation

theorem isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage_preservesKFlat
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} X.ProEt] [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} Y.ProEt]
    (RY : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (RX : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (isoSectionwiseInverseImage g CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj RY ≅ RX)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RY) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RX)) [F.Additive]
    (_hF : F = isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage.{u, u} g
      (RY := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RY)
      (RX := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RX)
      ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).mapIso c).hom) :
    ∀ K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RY)) ℤ,
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
        (J := ProEt.topology Y) (R := RY) K →
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
          (J := ProEt.topology X) (R := RX)
          ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
